title: Commercial LOS Replacement: Planning Kickoff
goals: Everyone understands the deadline and what it means working backward.
We agree on what we know, what we only think we know, and how we will check.
We make the first scope decision and name the people who will own this.
We leave with owners and dates for the next 30 days.

summary.lead: The group agreed to start now. GlobalWave is not a real option, small business lending is in scope, and we are aiming to go live in August 2028, about seven months before the contract ends on March 11, 2029.
heard: The biggest risks are data migration, integrations, and our own staff time, not just picking software.
We likely need a broader set of tools than a standalone LOS: fraud and KYC checks, digital workflow, and automation.
Abrigo and nCino are the main options. Abrigo looks promising and fits our current relationship; nCino is powerful but costly, rigid, and hard to fully adopt.
We are willing to change our processes to fit a good platform, apart from a few true non-negotiables.
LaserPro is likely staying for now.

slides.title: Replacing our commercial loan origination system

blocks.text: Today starts the planning for a new commercial LOS. Our contract with GlobalWave ends on March 11, 2029, and the replacement must be running well before then.

slides.notes: Welcome everyone. Explain that this meeting is a working session, not a vendor decision. We will walk through the deadline, what we know about the bank, what we think so far and what we still need to learn, then make a few early decisions. Everything we decide today gets recorded in this workspace.

slides.title: We have about 29 months. Most of it is already spoken for.

blocks.text: Working backward from March 11, 2029: we need a signed contract by late summer 2027 to implement, test and train before a go-live in August 2028. That leaves about seven months of buffer for surprises.

slides.notes: Make the point that 29 months sounds like a lot but selection alone typically takes 9-11 months, and implementation, testing and training another 11. The buffer is our insurance and we should protect it. Ask whether anyone knows of a non-renewal notice requirement in the GlobalWave contract; it may force a decision earlier than we expect.
discuss: Does anyone know the notice terms in the GlobalWave contract?
Are there blackout periods (exams, year-end, conversions) we must avoid in 2027-2028?

slides.title: A $3B bank planning for $5B, with a complex top end

blocks.text: Complex structures are under 10% of loans but 30% of committed dollars. The system has to make the standard deals fast without failing the complex ones.

slides.notes: These figures come from the Head of Commercial Lending and are treated as accurate. Highlight the two facts that shape the decision most: the complex 10% / 30% split, and the part-time administrator model. Any system that needs a full-time Salesforce admin or developer is a staffing decision as much as a software decision.
discuss: What does the complex 10% actually include? Participations, syndications, multi-tranche?
Is the part-time admin model staying, or could it change as we grow?
slides.capture: Corrections or additions to the bank profile

slides.kicker: Systems the LOS must work with
slides.title: The new LOS sits in the middle of four systems we keep
slides.notes: Every one of these integrations has to work on day one. The biggest open item is LaserPro: Finastra sold its US mid-market banking unit in June 2026 and may be sold entirely, so we need to confirm LaserPro's ownership and roadmap. Abrigo risk rating was recently onboarded, which is one reason Abrigo's own LOS is on the list.
discuss: Which of these integrations causes the most pain today?
Who owns the relationship with each vendor?

slides.title: Where we stand, and how sure we are

blocks.text: The only things we know for sure are about our own bank: our systems and our organization. Everything about vendors and cost is still a lead, not a fact. We have no real prices yet. Leads get confirmed through demos, reference calls, RFP pricing and our own experts.

slides.notes: We started from a draft assessment from September (prepared with an AI tool, Gemini) that compared Abrigo, GlobalWave and nCino. It raised the right topics: integration, admin burden, adoption and cost. But it picked a vendor before we had requirements, demos or references, so we are not walking through it line by line. Instead we turned it into what we think and how sure we are. A first check against public sources was done on October 2. Nothing about cost is known: every price we have is a placeholder until vendors quote in the RFP. One thing about us was settled: Section 1071 does not apply to the bank. No product called 'Abrigo APX' turned up.

slides.title: Questions we have to answer before we choose
slides.notes: Walk through each card briefly and confirm who owns it. These are the questions that most affect the choice. The full list, with how we'll answer each one, is on the What we need to learn page.
discuss: Is anything we think wrong, or missing?
Who should own each open question?

slides.title: What is in scope?
slides.notes: The question is whether small business lending ($250K-$500K) joins the commercial LOS project. The bank uses Numerated for it today, and whether Numerated stays is still open. Only the LOS is tied to the March 2029 deadline. The recommendation is option B: evaluate small business lending in the same RFP because it shares borrowers, credit policy and possibly the vendor, depending on Numerated's contract terms. Get a decision or a clear owner and date for one.
discuss: Is Numerated working well enough to keep?
Should we ask Abrigo for one platform covering both?
Would small business automation change how we staff credit?

slides.title: Is staying with GlobalWave on the table?
slides.notes: Even if we expect to leave, including the incumbent in the RFP gives us a cost baseline, negotiating leverage, and a fallback if a new implementation slips. It also means we should ask our own users what they think of Credit Track today rather than relying on the assessment's opinion.
discuss: Has leadership already decided to leave GlobalWave?
What would GlobalWave need to change for us to stay?

slides.title: Seven phases, three gates, one hard date
slides.notes: Walk left to right. Phases overlap on purpose. The gates that matter most: requirements signed off by March 31, 2027; contract signed by August 31, 2027; go/no-go in mid-July 2028. Ask the group to react to the target go-live of August 1, 2028 (Decision D04, to confirm by December).
discuss: Is an August 2028 go-live realistic for lending and loan ops?
What would make us miss the August 2027 contract gate?

slides.title: Agree on what matters before we see any demos
slides.notes: These weights are a starting suggestion. We will finalize them by the end of March 2027, before any vendor demo, so a polished demo does not reset our priorities. Integrations and admin burden are weighted heavily because of the part-time admin model. The CLO and PM panel scores usability directly.
discuss: What is missing from this list?
Who should sit on the CLO and PM user panel?

slides.title: Who owns this?
slides.notes: This is the most important decision today. Projects like this fail most often from unnamed owners and borrowed time. Get an executive sponsor and a project lead named, and agree on time commitments. Fill in names live if you can; anything unfilled becomes an action item.
discuss: Who is the executive sponsor?
Who is the project lead, and what comes off their plate?
Do we need temporary help for the part-time admin during implementation?

slides.title: Top risks we will manage from day one
slides.notes: Pick two or three to discuss. The GlobalWave notice terms and admin capacity are the ones most likely to surprise us.
discuss: Which risk worries you most?
What risk is missing?

slides.title: What happens after today
slides.notes: Read through each action and confirm an owner and date. Agree on the next meeting. Remind everyone that this workspace is the single place for decisions, what we think, open questions, risks and the plan, and that it will be kept current.
discuss: Are the owners and dates right?
When is the first core team meeting?
